av_event.line_text: Gemma: Oh, the phone's my favourite bit! Calming people down. I get lads ringing up shouting about where their tower is, and I just say, right, let's have a look.
av_event.what: In the bottom corner of the frame, the black Labrador's tail starts thumping in the dog bed. Then the dog stands up, stretches, and walks out of shot behind Gemma towards the fridge.

text:
A: Hiya! I'm Gemma. How's your day going?
B: Hi, I'm Lauren. Erm, it's okay, thanks. A bit tired. How's yours?
A: Oh, not bad, ta. Last one now! Where are you?
B: Basingstoke.
A: Oh, lovely. I'm Warrington. Sorry, I've said that about five times today.
B: Ha, me too. Basingstoke, Basingstoke.
A: What do you do, love?
B: I'm a vet nurse. Small animals.
A: Oh, are you? You'd have loved me last month, then. Bonnie, my Labrador, ate a whole sock. Sunday night, emergency vet, the lot.
B: Oh no. Did it come up, or did she need surgery?
A: They gave her something to make her sick and up it came. Craig's sock, of course. He leaves everything on the floor, boots, socks, all of it.
B: That's the best outcome, honestly. Labs are the worst for socks. We had one last year who'd eaten three. Sorry, I probably shouldn't say that.
A: Three! Oh, don't tell her, she'll take it as a challenge. Was he alright?
B: Yeah, he was fine in the end. It was a long surgery, though. I was monitoring the anaesthetic, so I was sort of on edge the whole time.
A: I couldn't do that, I'd be a wreck. I just do paperwork, admin for a scaffolding firm.
B: That still sounds hard. I hate doing reception cover, the phone and everything.
A: Oh, the phone's my favourite bit! Calming people down. I get lads ringing up shouting about where their tower is, and I just say, right, let's have a look.
B: I'd panic. I'm better with the animals than the owners.
A: Well, I bet you calm them down without even knowing it. What do you do when you're not working?
B: Erm, cross-stitch, reading. Baking sometimes, for people's birthdays at work.
A: Oh, I bake for work birthdays! Victoria sponge, usually. And for church fundraisers. What do you make?
B: Brownies mostly, because they're easy to cut up and they last. Do you watch Bake Off?
A: Religiously. I cry every single week. Craig thinks I'm mad, crying at a sponge.
B: I cry at the hugs. And when Paul does the handshake.
A: Oh, the handshake! I'm not even going to apologise for that one. Do you batch cook as well? You look like an organised one.
B: Sort of. On my days off. Chilli, pasta bake, soup, in labelled tubs. It saves money, which we sort of need at the minute.
A: Oh, I know. The big shop at Asda's gone silly. I do a chilli and a lasagne for the freezer, and scouse when it's cold. Do you eat early? We have tea on the table by six.
B: Erm, it depends on my shift. If I'm on lates it's dinner at about nine. I just have a tub out the freezer.
A: Oh, that's late, bless you. You need someone looking after you.
B: My mum does Sunday dinner most weeks, so that sort of covers it.
A: Ah, that's lovely. My mum's only ten minutes away and all. I pop round most days since, well, since we lost my dad. Sorry, I don't know why I
